**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the terminal offset outside Uint32 storage**

When `end - start` is `2 ** 32`, this write coerces the new terminal offset to `0` because `offsets` is a `Uint32Array`. This is a valid reachable fixed-size encoding under the repository's Node 24 target—for example, `new ListCompositeType(new ByteVectorType(2 ** 32), 1)` can receive one 4-GiB buffer without any serialized length offsets—but both deserialize loops now pass `[0, 0)` to the element and reject it, whereas the previous last-element branch passed the numeric `end`. Store the trailing end in full-width number storage (or retain the raw `end`) so the final range does not wrap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
